title_en: Jiangsu Zhongxun Digital Electronics Co., Ltd. v. Shandong Bit Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damage caused by maliciously filing an intellectual property lawsuit
ruling_gist_en: Where an actor, knowing that the disputed trademark has been previously used by another person and has acquired certain influence, preemptively registers the disputed trademark, the trademark right obtained thereby does not have substantive legitimacy. If the actor then files a trademark infringement lawsuit against a related party authorized by the prior user, such litigation shall be deemed as maliciously filing an intellectual property lawsuit. If such acts cause damage to others, the actor shall bear liability for damages.

full_text_en:
Jiangsu Zhongxun Digital Electronics Co., Ltd. v. Shandong比特 Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damage caused by maliciously instituting intellectual property litigation

Ruling Summary

Where an actor, knowing that a disputed trademark has been previously used by another party and has a certain level of influence, preemptively registers the disputed trademark, the trademark rights obtained thereby lack substantive legitimacy. If the actor subsequently initiates trademark infringement litigation against an affiliate licensed by the prior user, such litigation shall be deemed as maliciously instituted intellectual property litigation. If such conduct causes damage to others, liability for damages shall be borne.

Plaintiff: Jiangsu Zhongxun Digital Electronics Co., Ltd., domiciled at Tangshu Road, Dingshu Town, Yixing City, Jiangsu Province.

Legal Representative: Fan Xiaofeng, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

Defendant: Shandong比特 Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd., domiciled at Rizhao North Road, Rizhao City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Cao Xiangui, Chairman of the Board of the Company.

The Plaintiff, Jiangsu Zhongxun Digital Electronics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongxun Company), filed an action with the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province against the Defendant, Shandong比特 Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as 比特 Company), for a dispute over liability for damage caused by maliciously instituting intellectual property litigation.

Plaintiff's Allegations:

Zhongxun Company alleges that it was an OEM manufacturer in China for hotel telephones bearing the "TELEMATRIX" brand of the U.S. company Mitei Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Mitei Company). The Defendant, 比特 Company, was also formerly an OEM manufacturer for Mitei Company in China and was originally named Shandong比特 Electronics Industry Co., Ltd., which changed to its current name on February 22, 2016. In January 2008, 比特 Company sent a lawyer's letter to Zhongxun Company, claiming that it owned the exclusive right to use the "TELEMATRIX" trademark (Registration No. 435950, with designated goods including telephones), alleging that Zhongxun Company's promotion, production, and sale of telephone products bearing the "TELEMATRIX" trademark constituted trademark infringement, and demanding that Zhongxun Company cease such activities. In March 2008, 比特 Company filed a lawsuit with the Rizhao Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province against Zhongxun Company for infringement of the aforementioned registered trademark, seeking an injunction and damages. The case was subsequently transferred to the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province for jurisdiction in November 2008, and during the trial, 比特 Company claimed damages of RMB 6.12 million. 比特 Company also filed a complaint with the industrial and commercial authorities in August 2008, requesting an investigation and sanctions against Zhongxun Company. In November 2009, 比特 Company withdrew the lawsuit on the grounds of needing new evidence, which was permitted by the court. Under pressure from 比特 Company, Zhongxun Company was forced to terminate its OEM cooperation with Mitei Company regarding "TELEMATRIX" brand telephones, resulting in the scrapping of a large number of products and materials. The above conduct of 比特 Company caused significant losses to Zhongxun Company's production and operations. Subsequently, the Beijing High People's Court, in litigation, lawfully revoked the aforementioned trademark registration of 比特 Company and determined in its judgment that 比特 Company's registration constituted a preemptive registration of a trademark that was already in use by a partner and had a certain influence, through improper means, thus lacking legitimacy. 比特 Company applied for retrial to the Supreme People's Court, which lawfully found its conduct unlawful and dismissed the retrial application. At this point, it has become a legal fact that 比特 Company's registration of the trademark constituted unlawful conduct by improper means, and its trademark right never existed ab initio. Therefore, its lawsuit against Zhongxun Company constituted malicious litigation with egregious circumstances, damaging Zhongxun Company's reputation in the industry, causing Zhongxun Company to lose significant business opportunities, and resulting in substantial economic losses. Accordingly, Zhongxun Company requests the court to order 比特 Company: 1. to compensate Zhongxun Company for losses of RMB 6.12 million and reasonable expenses of RMB 100,000, and to eliminate the adverse effects in national media; 2. to bear the litigation costs of this case.

Defendant's Defense:

比特 Company argues: 1. The lawsuit filed by 比特 Company was a normal civil litigation and did not meet any elements of malicious litigation. Although the involved trademark was revoked, this does not indicate that the trademark infringement lawsuit filed during the validity period of the trademark was malicious. After a trademark is declared invalid, it generally has no retroactive effect on acts including prior trademark infringement litigation. Furthermore, 比特 Company filed the lawsuit based on the then-stable valid status of the trademark, without taking any preservation measures in the litigation, and had no subjective fault, nor did it cause any loss to the Plaintiff Zhongxun Company. 2. All evidence submitted by Zhongxun Company cannot prove that 比特 Company engaged in malicious litigation and is irrelevant. The alleged huge losses of Zhongxun Company lack factual and legal basis, and regardless of whether it suffered economic losses, they are unrelated to 比特 Company's litigation conduct.

Facts Found by the Wuxi Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province at First Instance:

From 1998 to 2003, 比特 Company's predecessor, Yankuang Group Shandong比特 Electronics Company (hereinafter referred to as Yankuang比特 Company), acted as an OEM manufacturer in China for U.S. company Satec Electronic Communication Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Satec Company), processing hotel-specific telephones for Satec Company under its commission. The cooperation between the parties did not involve telephones bearing the "TELEMATRIX" trademark. On March 28, 2006, Satec Company merged with TELEMATRIX INC. (Florida) and adopted "TELEMATRIX" as its corporate name, becoming TELEMATRIX INC. (Delaware), later renamed Mitei Corporation. Mitei Corporation authorized Beijing Mitei Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Beijing Mitei Company) to be the exclusive distributor in China for "TELEMATRIX" hotel-specific telephone products. Starting in 2006, Zhongxun Company, under the commission of Satec Company, processed hotel telephone products including those under the "TELEMATRIX" brand. A business statistics table and tax refund documents submitted by Zhongxun Company during the litigation showed that from 2006 to 2007, the gross profit from Zhongxun Company's OEM processing of "TELEMATRIX" brand hotel telephones was RMB 12,504,594.

On November 12, 2004, Yankuang比特 Company applied to the State Trademark Office for registration of the "TELEMATRIX" trademark, with designated goods in Class 9, including telephones, video phones, cordless telephones, network communication equipment, facsimile machines, complete cordless telephone sets, mobile phones, etc. On May 28, 2007, the trademark was registered, with a validity period from May 28, 2007, to May 27, 2017, under Registration No. 4359350. Thereafter, Yankuang比特 Company underwent two name changes and is now named 比特 Company. On its website, 比特 Company published the following promotional content: "As one of the three major hotel telephone brands internationally renowned alongside Teledex and TELEMATRIX, 比特 has always pursued leadership in products and services and is an innovator in many technologies and functions."

On January 8, 2008, 比特 Company, through a commissioned law firm, issued a lawyer's letter to Zhongxun Company, stating that Zhongxun Company's promotion, production, and sale of telephone products bearing the "TELEMATRIX" trademark in the *China Hotel Purchasing News* allegedly infringed upon 比特 Company's trademark rights and legitimate interests. The letter demanded that Zhongxun Company withdraw all related advertisements and promotions and cease all other related production, sales, import, and export activities, failing which legal action would be taken.

On March 28, 2008, Zhongxun Company filed a lawsuit with the Wuxi Intermediate Court seeking a declaration of non-infringement of 比特 Company's "TELEMATRIX" trademark rights. Thereafter, 比特 Company immediately filed a trademark infringement lawsuit with the Rizhao Intermediate Court, requesting an order that Zhongxun Company immediately cease its infringement of 比特 Company's registered trademark rights and pay damages. In November 2008, the Rizhao Intermediate Court transferred the case to the Wuxi Intermediate Court for trial. During the trial, 比特 Company expressly demanded that Zhongxun Company pay damages of RMB 6.12 million. On October 30, 2009, the Wuxi Intermediate Court issued civil rulings [(2008) Xi Min San Chu Zi No. 70-1 and (2009) Xi Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 57] respectively, granting permission for Zhongxun Company and 比特 Company to withdraw their lawsuits.

On August 21, 2008, the Yixing Municipal Industrial and Commercial Bureau, based on a complaint from 比特 Company, inspected the workshops and warehouses of Zhongxun Company and inventoried telephone products suspected of trademark infringement. Zhongxun Company stated that after 比特 Company filed the lawsuit, it ceased using the "TELEMATRIX" trademark on its products, replaced molds, and incurred expenses for scrapping telephone housings, trademark material losses, and labor costs for replacing telephone housings. A mold contract submitted by Zhongxun Company showed that in 2008, it commissioned a third party to manufacture molds for the upper and lower covers of telephones, with a total expenditure of RMB 83,000.

In August 2010, 比特 Company filed a lawsuit against Beijing Mitei Company, alleging that Beijing Mitei Company, without authorization, used "TELEMATRIX" as a trade name and telephone product name on its website and in promotional and sales activities, thereby infringing the aforementioned trademark rights. 比特 Company sought an injunction and damages. On September 6, 2010, Beijing Mitei Company filed a petition with the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce (hereinafter referred to as the TRAB) to revoke 比特 Company's "TELEMATRIX" trademark. On July 22, 2013, the TRAB issued a ruling finding that prior to the filing date of the disputed trademark application, TELEMATRIX INC. had applied for and registered the "TELEMATRIX" trademark in the European Union and other regions for goods such as telephones, and its "TELEMATRIX" hotel-specific telephone products had been recognized and used by numerous global hotel chain groups, achieving a certain degree of worldwide recognition, particularly within the U.S. hotel telephone industry. Furthermore, the evidence on record showed that in 2002, "TELEMATRIX" telephone products had already entered the Chinese hotel market. 比特 Company had cooperated with Mitei Company's predecessor, Satec Company, since 1998, engaging in the OEM processing of hotel-specific telephones. Although the trademark involved in the cooperation agreement was not the "TELEMATRIX" trademark, 比特 Company, as a partner in the same industry, should have been aware of the well-known brand that Mitei Company had registered and used internationally since 1998. Moreover, 比特 Company's own website acknowledged that "TELEMATRIX" was an internationally known hotel telephone brand of another party. 比特 Company's application for registration of a disputed trademark with identical text on identical or similar goods such as telephones can hardly be considered made in good faith, and it constituted the circumstance referred to in Article 31 of the Trademark Law regarding "preemptive registration by improper means of a trademark already used by another party and having a certain influence." Accordingly, the TRAB ruled to revoke the disputed trademark.

比特 Company, dissatisfied with the above ruling, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court. On December 19, 2013, the Beijing First Intermediate Court issued Administrative Judgment [(2013) Yi Zhong Zhi Chu Chu Zi No. 2956], finding that 比特 Company had cooperated with Mitei Company's predecessor since 1998, engaging in the processing of hotel telephones. As a specialized company, 比特 Company should have had some knowledge of the industry, particularly regarding the products of its cooperation partner. Moreover, 比特 Company's website promotional material showed that it acknowledged the fame of the "TELEMATRIX" trademark for hotel telephone products. The evidence on record demonstrated that the influence of the "TELEMATRIX" trademark was sufficient to reach 比特 Company and sufficient to prompt 比特 Company to preemptively register it to obtain benefits. Therefore, the registration of the disputed trademark violated the provision of Article 31 of the Trademark Law regarding preemptive registration by improper means of a trademark already used by another party and having a certain influence. The judgment thus upheld the TRAB's ruling. 比特 Company appealed, and the Beijing High Court issued Administrative Judgment [(2014) Gao Xing Zhong Zi No. 799] on March 21, 2014, dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment. 比特 Company applied for retrial with the Supreme People's Court regarding the effective judgment, and the Supreme People's Court ruled on December 15, 2014, to dismiss 比特 Company's retrial application.

The dispute focus of this case is: Whether the trademark infringement lawsuit filed by 比特 Company against Zhongxun Company constituted malicious litigation.

Opinion of the Court (Wuxi Intermediate People's Court, First Instance):

This case concerns a dispute related to malicious litigation in the context of intellectual property. To determine malicious intent, the following factors should be considered: First, the civil lawsuit was filed without factual basis and legitimate reason, i.e., the plaintiff did not have a valid legal basis for instituting the intellectual property litigation; Second, the purpose was to damage the legitimate rights and interests of others, i.e., subjective malice; Third, damage was caused to others, i.e., economic loss or weakening of competitive advantage.

Regarding the first point: At the time 比特 Company filed the lawsuit against Zhongxun Company, although it had obtained registration of the "TELEMATRIX" trademark, the TRAB subsequently, in the proceedings for revocation of the trademark, found that 比特 Company had preemptively registered a trademark already used by another party with a certain influence by improper means and accordingly revoked the trademark. 比特 Company challenged this ruling through administrative litigation, which was finally upheld by the courts after first and second instance trials. The "TELEMATRIX" trademark was thus revoked. Article 31 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (as amended in 2001) provides that no application for trademark registration may infringe upon another party's existing prior rights, nor may a trademark already used by another party and having a certain influence be preemptively registered by improper means. Article 41 provides that a registered trademark that violates Articles 10 or 11 of this Law, or was obtained by deceptive or other improper means, shall be revoked by the Trademark Office; other entities or individuals may request the TRAB to rule on the revocation of such a registered trademark. A registered trademark that violates Articles 13, 15, 16, or 31 of this Law may, within five years from the date of registration, be requested for revocation by the trademark owner or interested party. For malicious registration, the well-known trademark owner is not subject to the five-year limitation. Article 36, paragraph 1, of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (implemented in 2002) provides that for a registered trademark revoked in accordance with Article 41 of the Trademark Law, the exclusive right to use the trademark shall be deemed never to have existed from the beginning. Therefore, the "TELEMATRIX" trademark was registered by 比特 Company through improper means and ultimately revoked; in terms of legal effect, it is deemed null and void ab initio.  比特 Company essentially did not hold the exclusive right to use the "TELEMATRIX" trademark during the period from its registration to its final revocation. Accordingly, it can be determined that 比特 Company lacked a valid legal basis when it filed the No. 57 lawsuit.

Regarding the second point: Article 36 of the Implementing Regulations of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China (implemented in 2002) also provides that the decision or ruling on revocation of a registered trademark shall have no retroactive effect on judgments or rulings on trademark infringement cases that have been made by a people's court and executed before the revocation, on decisions on trademark infringement cases that have been made and executed by the administrative department for industry and commerce, or on trademark assignment or license contracts that have already been performed. However, compensation shall be made for losses caused to others by the malicious conduct of the trademark registrant. It can be seen from the above provisions that where the "TELEMATRIX" trademark has been revoked, if 比特 Company filed the No. 57 lawsuit maliciously, it may bear liability for damages. So-called malice is the subjective state of a party at the time of acting. Although it is impossible to fully trace and explore the party's inner state of mind at that time, the people's court may still comprehensively determine whether the party had malice based on the specific conduct of the party and other facts. In this case, if there is evidence proving that 比特 Company preemptively registered a trademark that had been put into commercial use by another party but not yet registered in time, and then filed an infringement lawsuit against the prior user based on its registered trademark rights, with the intention of damaging the prior user's interests under the guise of trademark rights enforcement, it can be determined that the party had subjective malice at the time of filing the lawsuit. First, according to the valid administrative judgment in the related case, 比特 Company applied for registration of the "TELEMATRIX" trademark, which had been previously used by another party with considerable fame and influence, as its own trademark. This conduct was clearly illegitimate and falls under one of the revocable circumstances provided by law. At the same time, 比特 Company's own website explicitly recognized that "TELEMATRIX" is an internationally known hotel telephone brand, thus proving that it registered the word as a trademark knowing that "TELEMATRIX" was a well-known trademark previously used by another party. Its application for registration was contrary to good faith and of evident malice. This malicious conduct is of significant importance for determining whether the involved lawsuit constitutes malicious litigation. Second, after obtaining the trademark registration, 比特 Company sent a lawyer's letter to Zhongxun Company, also an OEM manufacturer for Mitei Company, demanding that Zhongxun Company withdraw all advertisements and promotions related to "TELEMATRIX" telephones and cease all other related production, sales, import, and export activities, otherwise legal action would be taken. After Zhongxun Company filed a lawsuit for non-infringement, 比特 Company immediately filed a separate lawsuit seeking an injunction and damages. From the above facts, it can be seen that after maliciously obtaining the trademark registration, 比特 Company, in its capacity as the trademark owner, threatened Zhongxun Company to cease production and sale of the corresponding products, and ultimately filed the infringement lawsuit, attempting to pressure Zhongxun Company into refusing relevant commissions and stopping its OEM production activities, thereby controlling the production and sale of goods bearing the "TELEMATRIX" trademark in the domestic market and obtaining illegal profits thereby. As mentioned above, "TELEMATRIX" is an internationally known hotel telephone brand that had been registered in the European Union and other regions. Zhongxun Company's acceptance of a commission to process telephone products under this brand was legitimate. Therefore, although 比特 Company filed the lawsuit after Zhongxun Company had filed a declaratory judgment action, its substantive purpose remained to damage the legitimate rights and interests of Zhongxun Company, constituting abuse of rights through malicious exercise of trademark rights, which, like its conduct of malicious trademark registration, also lacks legitimacy. In this case, 比特 Company obtained registration of the disputed trademark through improper means contrary to the principle of good faith, and on this basis, with the intent to damage the legitimate rights and interests of the prior user, utilized litigation to maliciously exercise its rights. Accordingly, it should be determined that 比特 Company's conduct in filing the involved lawsuit constitutes abuse of rights and amounts to malicious litigation.

Regarding the third point, the lawsuit filed by Bit Co. would negatively impact the production and operation of Zhongxun Co., and Zhongxun Co.’s business opportunities from accepting the commissioned processing of “TELEMATRIX” telephone products would inevitably be lost. Therefore, the lawsuit in question damaged the legitimate rights and interests of Zhongxun Co. and caused it economic losses, for which Bit Co. shall bear liability for compensating the losses. The issue of damages in this case may refer to the application of the statutory damages method unique to intellectual property law, i.e., the people’s court shall determine the amount of damages by comprehensively considering relevant factors within a certain limit. Specifically, the court comprehensively considered factors such as Bit Co.’s subjective malice, Zhongxun Co.’s mold costs, material losses, reasonable portion of labor costs for replacing casings, and attorney fees paid by Zhongxun Co. for this case. Bit Co.’s malicious litigation caused adverse effects on Zhongxun Co., and Zhongxun Co.’s claim for Bit Co. to publicly eliminate the adverse effects is supported.

Accordingly, the Wuxi Intermediate People’s Court of Jiangsu Province, pursuant to Article 106, Paragraph 2, Article 134, Paragraph 1, Items (7) and (9), and Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People’s Republic of China, and Article 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, rendered the following judgment on July 26, 2017:

1. Shandong Bit Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. shall publish a statement to eliminate adverse effects in the *Legal Daily* within thirty days from the effective date of this judgment (the content must be reviewed by the court); if it fails to do so, the court shall select a media outlet to publish the content of the judgment, with the costs borne by Shandong Bit Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd.;

2. Shandong Bit Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. shall compensate Jiangsu Zhongxun Digital Electronic Co., Ltd. for economic losses and reasonable expenses amounting to RMB 1,000,000 within ten days from the effective date of this judgment;

3. Other claims of Jiangsu Zhongxun Digital Electronic Co., Ltd. are dismissed.

Bit Co. appealed the first-instance judgment to the Jiangsu High People’s Court, requesting: 1. Reversal of the first-instance judgment; 2. Confirmation that the lawsuit filed by Bit Co., Case No. (2009) Xi Zhi Min Chu Zi No. 57 (hereinafter referred to as Case No. 57), did not constitute malicious litigation, and dismissal of all claims of Zhongxun Co.; 3. Zhongxun Co. to bear the litigation costs of both the first and second instances. Grounds: 1. The first-instance judgment erroneously determined that Bit Co. acted with malice when applying for registration of the “TELEMATRIX” trademark and filing Case No. 57. The key factor in determining whether a party acted with malice in filing a lawsuit is whether the party subjectively knew it had no legal basis at the time of filing. The first-instance judgment failed to consider whether the party had subjective knowledge. (a) When Bit Co. filed Case No. 57, it held a valid registration certificate for the “TELEMATRIX” trademark and had reason to believe that Case No. 57 had a legal basis, thus lacking subjective malice. (b) When Bit Co. applied to register the “TELEMATRIX” trademark on November 12, 2004, it was unaware that “TELEMATRIX” had already been used by others (in China) and had acquired certain influence. The publicity on Bit Co.’s website only indicated that Bit Co. was aware at the time that “TELEMATRIX” was a foreign brand, but did not prove that Bit Co., when applying to register the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, knew that the mark had already been used by others (in China) and had acquired certain influence. (c) The first-instance judgment’s retroactive presumption that Bit Co. acted with malice when applying for registration and filing the lawsuit, simply because the “TELEMATRIX” trademark was subsequently cancelled, lacks factual and legal basis. 2. The first-instance judgment failed to consider important factors such as Zhongxun Co.’s dereliction in exercising its rights, Bit Co.’s restraint during the litigation, and the parties’ disposition of their litigation rights. (a) From the registration of the “TELEMATRIX” trademark until the filing of Case No. 57, nearly four years elapsed, during which Zhongxun Co. did not challenge the rights to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark in any way, constituting a failure to exercise its rights and should bear the corresponding consequences. (b) Bit Co. filed Case No. 57 only after Zhongxun Co. filed a lawsuit for a declaration of non-infringement; it was not initiated by Bit Co. voluntarily. Sending the lawyer’s letter to Zhongxun Co. was based on a legitimate exercise of rights founded on the “TELEMATRIX” trademark rights, not an exploitation of litigation to harm the other party’s legitimate interests. Throughout Case No. 57, Bit Co. exhibited restraint and rationality, not an abuse of litigation rights or malicious litigation. (c) The first-instance judgment should respect the parties’ freedom to dispose of their litigation rights. When Zhongxun Co. withdrew its lawsuit for a declaration of non-infringement, Bit Co. simultaneously withdrew Case No. 57, and the Wuxi Intermediate Court approved the withdrawal. Thus, Case No. 57 had been concluded, and the dispute between the parties had been resolved. Allowing one party to later renege and challenge the previously withdrawn lawsuit would undermine the seriousness of the litigation process. 3. The amount of damages determined in the first-instance judgment lacks factual and legal basis. (a) The first-instance judgment failed to ascertain the direct causal relationship between the damages claimed by Zhongxun Co., such as mold replacement costs, material losses, and labor costs for replacing casings, and Case No. 57. The first-instance judgment merely relied on the fact that the mold contracts and other expenses submitted by Zhongxun Co. fell within the period of Case No. 57 to conclude that such mold costs and other expenditures should be considered losses suffered due to Case No. 57, which lacks factual and legal basis. From an evidentiary standpoint, the material losses and labor costs for replacing casings claimed by Zhongxun Co. are insufficient to establish a sufficiently close connection with Case No. 57. However, the first-instance judgment, relying solely on “the possibility of replacing the casings of inventory products bearing the ‘TELEMATRIX’ trademark,” determined that such losses formed part of the damages, which does not satisfy the causation requirement under tort law. (b) The cooperation agreement between Saide Co. and Zhongxun Co. stipulated that the molds were to be provided by Saide Co., so Zhongxun Co. is not the proper party entitled to claim the costs of replacing molds. The first-instance judgment’s award of RMB 1,000,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses lacks factual and legal basis, the specific calculation method is unclear, and the amount is excessive.

The appellee, Zhongxun Co., argued in its defense: Bit Co.’s filing of Case No. 57 constituted malicious intellectual property litigation. 1. Bit Co. had no legal or factual basis for filing Case No. 57. The “TELEMATRIX” trademark was registered by Bit Co. through improper means and was ultimately cancelled. As a matter of law, it is deemed invalid from the outset, meaning Bit Co. did not enjoy the exclusive right to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark throughout the period from its registration to its cancellation. 2. Bit Co. exhibited obvious subjective malice in filing Case No. 57 against Zhongxun Co. (a) Both the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board and the courts at three levels have determined that Bit Co. preemptively registered a trademark that others had already used and acquired certain influence, through improper means. Furthermore, as a professional company and operator in the same industry, Bit Co. should have had knowledge of the industry, especially regarding its partners’ products. Bit Co.’s website expressly stated that “TELEMATRIX” was an internationally renowned hotel telephone brand of others. These facts demonstrate that Bit Co. already exhibited very clear subjective malice when applying for registration of the “TELEMATRIX” trademark. (b) Bit Co. exhibited very clear malice when filing Case No. 57. First, Bit Co.’s subjective purpose in filing the lawsuit was not to genuinely protect legitimate rights and interests. The state of subjective malice at the time of trademark application is significant for determining the subjective state of mind at the time of filing Case No. 57. The evidence in this case can prove that Bit Co., knowing that the “TELEMATRIX” trademark was owned by others and that it had not obtained substantial legitimate rights to the trademark, actively filed the lawsuit with the aim of harming a competitor’s interests, showing clear subjective malice. Before the date of registration of the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, Bit Co. already knew that the true owner of the trademark was its former partner. Thus, Bit Co. not only exhibited clear subjective malice in filing Case No. 57 against Zhongxun Co., but also had subjective malice when it sent the lawyer’s letter threatening legal action against Zhongxun Co. Additionally, Bit Co. not only filed a lawsuit against Zhongxun Co., but also filed lawsuits against the true owner, Beijing Marquis Grand Co. (established by Marquis Grand Inc., USA), another OEM in China, and two downstream distributors. It also simultaneously took measures such as industry and commerce investigations and customs seizures, exceeding the reasonable scope of legitimate rights protection and constituting a series of planned malicious litigations. Bit Co.’s claim that it remained restrained and rational during Case No. 57 and related proceedings is inconsistent with the facts. 3. Bit Co.’s filing of Case No. 57 caused enormous losses to Zhongxun Co.’s production and operations. Zhongxun Co. was forced to replace molds, rework finished telephone products, and scrap labels, instruction manuals, packaging boxes, and packaging cases already produced bearing the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, resulting in huge material losses and labor costs. Bit Co.’s litigation also led to a sharp decline in Zhongxun Co.’s OEM orders, causing a rapid decrease in the expected substantial OEM profits, which persisted for a long period. At the same time, after Bit Co. obtained the registration of the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, it began to use it extensively, free-riding to reap enormous improper economic benefits, with total sales reaching nearly RMB 8,000,000. The first-instance court’s award of RMB 1,000,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses to Zhongxun Co. was not improper. In summary, the first-instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law; the appeal should be dismissed and the judgment affirmed.

After the second-instance trial, the Jiangsu High People’s Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The Jiangsu High People’s Court held in the second instance:

I. Bit Co.’s filing of the lawsuit in question constituted malicious intellectual property litigation. 1. Although Bit Co. ostensibly held the right to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark when it filed the lawsuit, such trademark right was obtained by “preemptively registering a trademark that others had already used and acquired certain influence, through improper means,” and Bit Co. did not possess a substantively legitimate basis of rights. The people’s court also rendered a final judgment cancelling the disputed trademark, and Bit Co.’s exclusive right to the trademark is deemed nonexistent from the outset. Therefore, when Bit Co. filed the lawsuit in question, it did not substantively hold the right to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark. 2. Bit Co. acted with subjective malice when filing the lawsuit in question. First, Bit Co. knew that the “TELEMATRIX” trademark was a mark that others had already used and had acquired certain influence, and it had preemptively registered it through improper means, exhibiting malice. It should have known that preemptively registering the “TELEMATRIX” trademark through improper means violated Article 31 of the Trademark Law and constituted a circumstance subject to cancellation. The facts also prove that the disputed trademark was ultimately cancelled. Therefore, Bit Co.’s appeal ground that “the company had no malice when applying for registration” lacks factual basis. Second, Bit Co. acted with malice when filing the lawsuit. Before filing the lawsuit in question, Bit Co. stated on its company website: “As one of the three major hotel telephone brands internationally, alongside Delida and TELEMATRIX, Bit has always pursued leadership in products and services.” This fact further confirms that after applying to register the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, Bit Co. was always aware that it had preemptively registered a mark that others had previously used and which had acquired certain influence. The right to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark should belong to the party that first used the mark and gradually accumulated goodwill, and Bit Co. should not substantively hold the right to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark. Meanwhile, since Zhongxun Co. and Bit Co. were both professional manufacturers of hotel telephone products, they were in a competitive relationship. Bit Co.’s filing of the lawsuit requesting Zhongxun Co. to cease production, sale, and promotion of products bearing the “TELEMATRIX” trademark was clearly aimed at excluding its competitor Zhongxun Co., monopolizing the domestic production and sale of products related to the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, harming Zhongxun Co.’s legitimate rights and interests, and obtaining illegal benefits. 3. Bit Co.’s filing of the lawsuit in question caused losses to Zhongxun Co., and there is a causal relationship between those losses and Bit Co.’s litigation conduct.

II. The first-instance court’s award of RMB 1,000,000 in economic losses and reasonable expenses to Zhongxun Co. was not improper. In this case, Bit Co.’s malicious filing of Case No. 57 caused economic losses to Zhongxun Co., and Bit Co. shall bear civil liability for compensating those losses. Malicious intellectual property litigation is essentially a type of tort. The amount of compensation to be paid by the perpetrator of malicious litigation shall be limited to the victim’s losses. Where the victim’s losses are difficult to ascertain, the court may comprehensively consider relevant factors and determine the amount of compensation at its discretion. Therefore, the first-instance court, having comprehensively considered Zhongxun Co.’s economic losses and Bit Co.’s malice and other factors, determined the amount of compensation, which was not improper.

III. After obtaining registration of the “TELEMATRIX” trademark, Bit Co., within a short period, successively sent warning letters to Zhongxun Co., filed a lawsuit, and made industry and commerce reports. Bit Co.’s appeal ground that “it remained restrained during the litigation” lacks factual basis. The withdrawal of the lawsuit in the aforementioned cases was not due to the parties reaching a settlement agreement. Zhongxun Co. did not waive its right to pursue Bit Co.’s liability for malicious litigation and is entitled to file this lawsuit in accordance with the law. Bit Co.’s appeal ground that the dispute between the parties had been resolved lacks factual basis.

In summary, the first-instance judgment found clear facts and correctly applied the law, and should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People’s Republic of China, the Jiangsu High People’s Court rendered the following judgment on September 28, 2018:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
